summary: Intermittent tail latency for short streaming requests during low steady QPS — timer drift in continuous coalescer
description:
Issue summary: Beginning 2024-11-12 11:40 UTC PixelFlow observed recurring p95/p99 latency spikes for short streaming requests (avg token count < 40). The spikes occur in bursts lasting 2-8 minutes every ~20-40 minutes and manifest as 504s and multi-second tails on otherwise idle connections.

Impact: Customer-facing inference endpoints experiencing degraded responsiveness for short chat turns. Affects automated UX tests and some billing-sensitive flows. Customer is on Dedicated capacity with reserved GPU pool.

Observed behavior:
- P95 increases from ~120ms to 600-1800ms; P99 hits 2.5s+ during bursts.
- Spikes coincide with small bursts of traffic following quiet periods.
- Streaming connections show delayed first-chunk emission despite model execution logs showing prompt token generation started on GPU.

Expected behavior:
- Low-latency first-chunk delivery for short-streaming requests even during low global QPS.

Relevant context:
- This tenant is pinned to a dedicated pool where continuous coalescer (our micro-batch/merge service) is enabled.
- Recent runtime change (timer refactor, release v1.14.2) was rolled to dedicated clusters on 2024-11-10.

Attachments: dashboard links and example request IDs included below.
steps_to_reproduce: Using tenant PixelFlow on prod us-east-1 with low sustained QPS (~3-6 rps), send short streaming requests (prompt+stop sequences resulting in < 40 tokens).
Observe response times over 30+ minutes; spikes replicate when low steady traffic is interspersed with small bursts (10-50 concurrent short requests).
Capture request IDs flagged during spike window and correlate with coalescer metrics and KV-cache hit rates.
investigation_notes: 11:50 UTC - Support triage: confirmed pattern shown in customer dashboards (p99 spike cadence ~ every 20-40m). Ticket escalated to SRE due to Sev1 impact.

12:05 UTC - SRE initial hypothesis: timer refactor in v1.14.2 may be increasing effective linger with low QPS due to race between coalescer timer and per-connection backpressure. Measured coalescer timer jitter in prod and saw outliers up to 12ms vs expected 1-3ms under idle load.
12:30 UTC - Experiment: forced coalescer linger floor to 1ms for tenant; immediate reduction in first-chunk tails observed in Canary cluster (p99 reduced by ~40%).

13:10 UTC - Observed correlation between KV-cache misses and larger delay; when KV cache cold, coalescer merges smaller batches which then sit for an extra timer interval before flush. This seems amplified by recent timer refactor where stale timer callbacks may be batched by the event loop.

13:50 UTC - Captured flamegraphs showing minor scheduling jitter in coalescer worker thread during GC cycles of sidecar; hypothesis: thread preemption + timer coalescing increases the effective linger on idle connections causing tail spikes for short requests.

Action items: 1) Rollback timer refactor on dedicated pools as a temporary mitigation. 2) Add per-tenant minimum flush floor and pre-warm KV cache on burst detect. 3) Postmortem + full regression test for streaming first-chunk latency.
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 2024-11-12T12:00Z: Customer reported first-chunk delays and intermittent 504s. Asked for request IDs and dashboards. Noted tenant is Dedicated and pinned to pool-id d-pool-9.

PixelFlow - Emma Liu (Customer) 2024-11-12T12:08Z: We see those spikes from our end around 11:40 UTC, attached two example request IDs: px-rt-9b2c, px-rt-9d7f. Impacting chat preview tests — can you escalate?

Marco Rossi (SRE) 2024-11-12T12:18Z: Escalating to Eng runtime team. Initial suspicion: coalescer timer drift in v1.14.2. Reproduced on a small dedicated test pool with synthetic short-stream workload.

Jin Park (Runtime Eng) 2024-11-12T13:25Z: Experiment applied - set coalescer linger_floor=1ms for tenant d-pool-9. Monitoring for 30m window. Noted immediate improvement in canary. Preparing rollback plan for v1.14.2 on dedicated pools.
Aisha Patel (Support) 2024-11-12T14:05Z: Shared mitigation steps with customer: enabled preemptive KV warmup and lowered linger floor. Customer to validate in next 2 hours and confirm UX metrics.
resolution: Mitigation deployed 2024-11-12 13:30 UTC: set per-tenant coalescer linger_floor=1ms and enabled KV-cache warmup on burst detect for PixelFlow's pool. Rolled back timer refactor v1.14.2 on dedicated pools pending full fix. Long-term fix tracked in PR #2184 (event-loop timer smoothing and worker preemption guards). Follow-up: postmortem and extended regression suite scheduled (owner: Jin Park, due 2024-11-20).
